title: Dubai's 'Invite' Scheme Offers $800 in Perks to Revive Post-War Tourism
excerpt: UAE residents who nominate overseas visitors arriving before October 31 can unlock hotel stays, attraction tickets, and dining deals worth over AED 3,000 — part of Dubai's aggressive push to rebuild its tourism brand after the Iran conflict.
body:
• Dubai's "A Dubai Invite" programme rewards UAE residents with benefits worth over AED 3,000 (~$816) for nominating overseas visitors arriving between July 20 and October 31, 2026.
  • Perks include free hotel nights at IHG properties, tickets to Aquaventure and IMG Worlds of Adventure, dining deals, and Careem transport credits.
  • The scheme is the latest move in Dubai's tourism recovery after hotel occupancy crashed from 80% to a projected 10% following missile strikes in March.
  • With over 700,000 Indian nationals living in the UAE, the programme offers a direct incentive for Indian residents to bring family and friends for summer visits.

Dubai is turning its own residents into tourism ambassadors. The Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) launched "A Dubai Invite" on July 20, a programme that rewards UAE residents and citizens with a package of perks worth more than AED 3,000 (approximately $816) each time they nominate an overseas visitor to come to the emirate.

The scheme — open to anyone aged 18 or older with a valid Emirates ID — allows residents to register up to three guests through an online nomination form on Visit Dubai's website. Once a nominated visitor arrives in Dubai between now and October 31, 2026, the resident receives an email with a benefits package redeemable until December 31.

What's in the Rewards Package

The benefits span hotels, attractions, dining, and transport. Hotel perks include a free night's stay at selected IHG properties, 45% off stays at Melia Desert Palm, 35% off rooms at ME Dubai by Meliá, and full room-rate credit at Destination Mina Seyahi. Attraction deals include free tickets to Aquaventure World and IMG Worlds of Adventure, plus 50% off at Grand Hyatt Dubai Waterpark.

Dining offers feature buy-one-get-one deals at restaurants including Asia Asia, Papas, The 305, and Lock, Stock & Barrel. Transport perks cover 20% off Careem Rides and Hala taxis, along with complimentary Careem Plus membership.

Each visitor can only be nominated once across the entire programme, and residents are capped at three benefit packages total.

A Tourism Sector in Recovery Mode

The invite programme arrives against a grim backdrop. Dubai logged a record 19.59 million international visitors in 2025, but the Iran conflict that erupted in late February devastated the tourism sector. Ballistic missile and drone strikes targeted the UAE in March, damaging landmarks including the Fairmont The Palm and the Jumeirah Burj Al Arab — which remains closed for an 18-month restoration. Dubai International Airport was temporarily shut, and carriers including British Airways and Emirates paused flights.

Hotel occupancy cratered from 80% to a projected 10% after the attacks, according to CNN. CoStar data shows occupancy bottomed out at 19.6% on March 15 before recovering to 82.2% by late May during Eid, then settling in the high 40s to low 50s through June.

"This is Dubai's ultimate nightmare as its very essence depended on being a safe oasis in a troubled region. There might be a way to be resilient but there is no going back."

— Cinzia Bianco, European Council on Foreign Relations

Dubai has pledged a cumulative AED 2.5 billion ($681 million) in support for tourism and retail, including suspending the nightly hotel tax at higher-end properties and removing the 7% municipal fee on hotel and restaurant bills. A Dh1.5 billion ($408 million) incentives package announced in May included exemptions from the tourism dirham fee and reduced fees for tour guides and desert safari operators.

Residents as Ambassadors

"At a time when personal connection and credibility matter more than ever in travel decisions, 'A Dubai Invite' speaks directly to what makes this city enduringly compelling: the people who call it home," Noor Al Geziry, AVP for Special Projects & MENA at DET, said in a statement.

The strategy is straightforward: leverage the trust that residents have with their personal networks abroad to counteract the reputational damage from months of conflict coverage. Travel warnings remain in place from several governments — the United States continues to urge travellers to reconsider trips to the UAE.

"I think it has created hesitation rather than fundamentally damaged confidence in the UAE itself. International audiences often view the Middle East as one broad region rather than distinguishing between countries."

— Naim Maadad, CEO, Gates Hospitality

What It Means for Indian Residents and Travellers

India is the UAE's largest source of expatriate workers, with over 700,000 Indian nationals living in Dubai alone. The invite programme creates a tangible incentive for Indian residents to bring family members over during the summer — traditionally a peak season for visiting friends and relatives (VFR) travel from India.

Indian passport holders are eligible for visa on arrival in the UAE, which simplifies the nomination process. The programme's July-to-October window aligns with Indian school holidays and the festive season buildup, when family visits are common.

For visitors from India considering a Dubai trip, the practical calculus is simple: a family member or friend already in the UAE registers their details before departure, and the resulting perks — free attraction tickets, hotel discounts, and dining deals — effectively subsidize the visit by several hundred dollars.

What's Next

Dubai's tourism authority has not released official visitor numbers since January, making the full scale of recovery difficult to gauge. More than 100 conferences and exhibitions were cancelled or postponed due to the conflict, and business travel has been slower to return than leisure. Whether word-of-mouth incentives can accelerate the rebound ahead of the crucial winter high season remains the open question — but for now, Dubai is betting that its residents are its most credible marketing channel.
nri_angle: Over 700,000 Indian nationals in Dubai can use the programme to bring family from India during peak VFR season, with visa-on-arrival eligibility simplifying the process.
